To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of 30 microg of ethinylestradial in combination with 2 mg of dienogest in a 21/7 day cycle, is a safe and effective contraceptive, with a good cycle control and an acceptable side effect profile.

the use of DNG containing OC caused a higher rise of serum binding globulin levels, while estradiol appeared to increase prolac tin release, and that the cycle control was best with the OC containing EE.
the use of DNG containing OC caused a higher rise of SHBG and TB G levels than the use of LNG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new contraceptive methods.
the development of new oral contraceptives with a lower dose of the synthetic estrogen ethinyl estradiol and with a new type of progestogen, estradiol.
the development of a new oral contraceptive containing 20 microg ethinyl estradiol (EE2) and 2 mg estrone sulfate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all OCs used in this study were well tolerated and effective, but the differences observed were not of clinical relevance.
the effects on the endocrine and metabolic parameters of the four OCs used in this study were not only due to the progestogens, but also to the estrogen components.
the effects of the different OCs on the various hormone levels are not only dependent on the dose and type of estrogen but also on the progestogen used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of 30 microg of ethinylestradial and 2mg of DNG in a monophasic oral contraceptive is a safe and effective method of contraception.
the DNG containing monophasic OCs are as well tolerated as the LNG containing OC, while the DNG containing products are superior to the EE/EV/DNS in terms of cycle control.

the DNG containing preparations showed a more pronounced effect on SHBG and TB G than the LNG containing formulation, which was associated with a better cycle control and a higher incidence of intracyclical bleeding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single best contraceptive for every patient.
the use of the DNG containing oral contraceptives caused a higher rise of SHBG and TBGs than the LNG containing preparations.
we need to think about the whole person and not just their disease.
